title: Fault-Level Table to Excel (openpyxl)
description: Write a multi-sheet Excel workbook of fault-level results from a Python dict. Includes column formatting, conditional fill for kA breaches, and a summary sheet with formulas — the kind of deliverable that goes straight into a connection-study report appendix.

blocks.text: Source data is a list of dicts (one per fault calc). Output workbook has one tab per fault type and a Summary tab that pulls the maxima with formulas. Cell rules highlight any fault current above the breaker rating.

from openpyxl import Workbook
from openpyxl.styles import Font, PatternFill, Alignment, Border, Side
from openpyxl.formatting.rule import CellIsRule
from openpyxl.utils import get_column_letter

FAULT_TYPES = ['3-phase', 'L-G', 'L-L', 'L-L-G']
BREAKER_KA  = 31.5  # rated symmetrical interrupting capability

results = [  # placeholder — replace with your real study output
    {'bus':  'A1', 'voltage_kV': 132, '3-phase': 28.4, 'L-G': 30.1, 'L-L': 24.6, 'L-L-G': 31.8},
    {'bus':  'A2', 'voltage_kV': 132, '3-phase': 22.1, 'L-G': 24.3, 'L-L': 19.1, 'L-L-G': 25.2},
    {'bus':  'B1', 'voltage_kV':  33, '3-phase':  9.4, 'L-G': 10.2, 'L-L':  8.1, 'L-L-G': 10.7},
]

wb = Workbook()
wb.remove(wb.active)

thin = Side(style='thin', color='AAAAAA')
border = Border(left=thin, right=thin, top=thin, bottom=thin)
header_fill = PatternFill('solid', fgColor='1F2937')
header_font = Font(bold=True, color='FFFFFF')
breach_fill = PatternFill('solid', fgColor='FECACA')

for ft in FAULT_TYPES:
    ws = wb.create_sheet(title=ft)
    ws.append(['Bus', 'Voltage (kV)', f'I_fault {ft} (kA)', 'Breaker (kA)', 'Margin (%)'])
    for cell in ws[1]:
        cell.fill = header_fill
        cell.font = header_font
        cell.alignment = Alignment(horizontal='center')

    for row, r in enumerate(results, start=2):
        ifault = r[ft]
        margin = (1 - ifault / BREAKER_KA) * 100
        ws.append([r['bus'], r['voltage_kV'], ifault, BREAKER_KA, round(margin, 1)])

    # Conditional fill: red where I_fault > breaker rating
    rng = f'C2:C{len(results) + 1}'
    ws.conditional_formatting.add(rng,
        CellIsRule(operator='greaterThan', formula=[str(BREAKER_KA)], fill=breach_fill))

    # Borders + autosize
    for col in range(1, ws.max_column + 1):
        for row in range(1, ws.max_row + 1):
            ws.cell(row=row, column=col).border = border
        max_len = max(len(str(ws.cell(row=r, column=col).value or ''))
                      for r in range(1, ws.max_row + 1))
        ws.column_dimensions[get_column_letter(col)].width = max_len + 4

# Summary tab — uses INDIRECT to reference each fault tab
summary = wb.create_sheet(title='Summary', index=0)
summary.append(['Bus', 'Max I_fault (kA)', 'Critical fault type'])
for cell in summary[1]:
    cell.fill = header_fill
    cell.font = header_font

for row, r in enumerate(results, start=2):
    summary.cell(row=row, column=1, value=r['bus'])
    summary.cell(row=row, column=2,
        value=f'=MAX({"\'3-phase\'!C"}{row},\'L-G\'!C{row},\'L-L\'!C{row},\'L-L-G\'!C{row})')
    summary.cell(row=row, column=3,
        value=f'=INDEX({{""3-phase"",""L-G"",""L-L"",""L-L-G""}},MATCH(B{row},'
              f'(\'3-phase\'!C{row},\'L-G\'!C{row},\'L-L\'!C{row},\'L-L-G\'!C{row}),0))')

wb.save('fault-level-study.xlsx')
print('Wrote fault-level-study.xlsx')

openpyxl writes pure XLSX without needing Excel installed. For interactive use (modifying an open workbook in real-time, recording macros) use xlwings instead — but xlwings requires Excel on the machine running the script.

Conditional formatting rules are written to the file but only visible AFTER Excel re-saves the file. On some machines the rule appears greyed out until you tap any cell. This is an Excel quirk, not an openpyxl bug.
